texts.preamble: M/S Sri Ram Food Industries vs H.P. State Civil Supplies Corporation on 10 October, 2017 Author: Chander Bhusan Barowalia Bench: Chander Bhusan Barowalia In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh At Shimla Arb. Case No.66 of 2017 Date of d e c i s i o n : 1 0 . 1 0 . 2 0 1 7 _____________________________________________________________ . M/s Sri Ram Food Industries ... Petitioner Versus H.P. State Civil Supplies Corporation ...Respondent. Coram: The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Chander Bhusan Barowalia, Judge. 1 Whether approved for reporting ?
texts.facts: This petition has been filed under sub-section (6) of Section 11 of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996 for appointment of Arbitrator. It has been alleged that Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment? Yes. respondent No.2 invited global tenders for the procurement of assorted pulses to be supplied to respondent No.2, for a period of three to six months, from June, 2016 onwards and the petitioner/firm (hereinafter to be referred as "the . petitioner") applied in pursuance of the abovementioned tender and being the lowest bidder, the petitioner was approved for arranging supplies of Daal Chana and Urad Whole to the respondents for which various supply orders were issued by the respondent-Corporation to the petitioner vide Annexure P-2 to P-9. r It has been alleged that the petitioner has diligently carried out the supplies of pulses, as per the respective supply orders, to various Godowns of respondent No.2/Corporation (hereinafter to be referred as "respondent No.2") during the continuance of the entire term of the tender document. It M/S Sri Ram Food Industries vs H.P. State Civil Supplies Corporation on 10 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155503683/ 1 has been alleged that respondent No.2, lifted some samples of pulses from the supplies made by the petitioner firm, which were failed. Thereafter, various recovery letters/notices alleged to have been sent to the petitioner by the respondent-Corporation and respondent No.2 recovered certain sums, as penalty from the amount payable by the respondent No.2 to the petitioner. The petitioner disputes the letters on various grounds including mode and method of sampling and analysis not being in accordance with mandatory provision of law and in violation of relevant rules. It has been alleged that neither the samples have been drawn in accordance with the provisions . of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act/ Food Safety and Standards Act and Rules made thereunder nor the same have been analyzed properly inasmuch as neither the petitioner has been associated in any manner by the Corporation at the time of drawing of the alleged samples nor the same have been drawn and analyzed according to the Food Safety and Standards Act. It has also been alleged that no test report has been attached with the said notices. It has been alleged that no reply to the legal notices was received and also that vide legal notice, dated 18.5.2017, the petitioner invoked arbitration clause in terms of Clause 14 of the Global Tender Form and requested respondent No.2- Corporation to appoint an Arbitrator.
texts.arguments: It has also been alleged that respondent No.1, has failed to make the payment to the petitioner and even failed to nominate its Arbitrator in terms of Clause 14 of the Global E Tender Form(Annexure P-1). Therefore, a prayer has been made to appoint an Arbitrator to adjudicate the dispute between the parties under the mandate of the provisions adumbrated in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. 3. Heard. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned vice counsel appearing for the petitioner has argued that an Arbitrator is . required to be appointed for adjudication of the dispute arisen between the parties, as the respondents/State have failed to appoint Arbitrator despite several requests and within the reasonable time, therefore, some other person may be appointed as Arbitrator. 4. rMr. Navlesh Verma, Advocate, for respondent No.1 has very fairly stated that, in case there is any dispute, Arbitrator may be appointed and respondent No.1 will maintain his claim before the Arbitrator. 5. Mr. Pushpender Jaswal, learned Deputy Advocate General appearing for the respondent No.2 has stated that in case there is disputed Arbitrator may be appointed for resolution of the dispute.
